name: Fast Parse — the Morph playbook on document-to-structure (one specialized VLM plus a page-shaped engine)
one_line: A one-model inference company serving document-page-to-markdown/JSON on a purpose-built vLLM-based engine (copy speculator, visual-token budgeter, page scheduler) priced per page; the only in-repo evidence is a buyer-replicable resize lever on 200 short-answer pages, and every Morph-specific mechanism is unmeasured.
evidence_grade_reason: The one in-engine measurement that touches this workload is real but bounded: Qwen2.5-VL-7B at 1024 px gives 2.7x throughput at -1.0 pt on 200 DocVQA pages (vLLM 0.24.0, A100, one run, max_tokens=32, one offline LLM.chat batch), and the ledger itself labels it a naive resize "a client can apply before any API" that "sizes the prize but isn't yet the moat". The accuracy-parity claim (0.925 vs GPT-4o 0.880) is ledger-status BOUNDED: the GPT-4o run output is unrecorded except that number, GPT-4o-mini is unrecorded, and GPT-4o is a 2024 comparator. Every Morph-playbook-specific mechanism the thesis rests on — copy fraction, copy speculation, a trained draft head, content-aware pruning (OPEN, blocked by Qwen2.5-VL mRoPE), the fine-tuned model, full-page parse throughput, and behavior under concurrency — is unmeasured in both repos (D on its own). C rather than D because the economics precondition was measured in-engine once; C rather than B because what was measured is explicitly not the differentiated claim and was never replicated or run on the product's actual output length.
build_cost_weeks_to_proof: 8-10 weeks to the first credible public proof of the engine claim (well-configured vLLM baseline vs engine v0 on full-page parse, olmOCR-Bench + DocVQA, 3 seeds, A100 + H100, public rerunnable harness), assuming 1-2 engineers, ~$3-5k of Modal GPU and frontier-API spend, that vLLM's speculative-decoding path accepts Qwen3-VL image inputs (unverified; not in the research files), and that the week-1 copy-fraction gate passes. 14-18 weeks if speculation must be built into the multimodal path (the week-2 slip risk) or if the fine-tuned model is part of the proof (~50k synthetic pages at ~$0.12 = ~$6k plus ~40 GPU-h, three weeks not one). The draft's 6 weeks assumed engine, fine-tune, load harness generalization, and three signed pilots with zero prior customer conversations in the repos.

attacks.attack: Combined engine-kill: if a well-configured vLLM (same max_pixels, FP8, prefix caching, built-in n-gram speculation with OCR text in the prompt) captures most of the gain AND the trained draft head adds little over n-gram, the 'purpose-built engine' has no measured advantage and the thesis reduces to a fine-tuned open VLM behind a per-page API — a product shape Reducto r-1, Mistral OCR 4 and the open OCR models already occupy (fact, not verdict). The ledger already says the 2.7x is a resize 'a client can apply before any API' and FINDINGS calls the VLM result 'copyable'.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Weeks 1-2: baseline (1) vs default vLLM pages/GPU-s at equal accuracy (kill if baseline (1) captures >= 80% of the engine gain) and trained draft head vs n-gram vs none single-stream s/page on 1,000 full-page parses (kill if < 1.5x over n-gram). Both gates fail = engine half dead; founder then decides whether a model-plus-pricing company is worth building.

attacks.attack: No full-page parse measurement exists anywhere in the repos. Every in-repo number is max_tokens=32 short-answer output from one offline LLM.chat batch of 200 images; the product's real workload is 300-800 output tokens per page, where decode dominates (~22 ms/step single-stream implies ~11 s per 500-token page before speculation) and the batch lane's economics depend on decode batching that was never measured. The $0.023/1K floor is field-QA only.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Prefill/decode split at 1024 px for 50/200/500-token outputs, then pages/GPU-s over HTTP at 300-800 output tokens, N = 8..256, 3 seeds, A100 and H100; COGS per 1K pages from measured pages/GPU-h. Kill gate 8: COGS > $5/1K.

attacks.attack: Copy speculation is unmeasured for documents and its off-the-shelf form is not proprietary: n-gram/prompt-lookup drafts ship in Baseten BIS-LLM and Together ATLAS, and vLLM has its own n-gram method. Morph's 3.07x-vs-1.93x is for code. For scanned pages there is no text layer, so the draft depends on CPU OCR quality; and speculative gains shrink at high batch as decode becomes compute-bound, so the batch metric cannot rely on it. The CUA analog shows 'redundancy' (86%) and 'realized speedup' (2.34x ceiling) can diverge widely.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Copy fraction on 1,000 pages split scanned vs native-text; acceptance length and s/page for trained head vs n-gram vs none at N=1 and N=64. Kill gate 1 (< 40% verbatim) and gate 4 (< 1.5x over n-gram).

attacks.attack: Version/API dependency: whether vLLM 0.24's speculative-decoding path accepts multimodal (Qwen3-VL image) inputs is not covered by any research file. If it does not, week 2 becomes an engine modification of unknown length — the same class of 'API cannot express it' wall the voice repo hit with the KVConnector and the dexa repo hit with Qwen2.5-VL mRoPE. The scheduler pattern (modal_verifier_sched.py) drives LLMEngine directly, so a new HTTP serving loop is also required.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Week-1 smoke test: enable n-gram speculation on the doc endpoint and confirm acceptances > 0 with identical greedy output; gate 4's '> 3 weeks to make the path work' kill. Same check on SGLang before choosing the engine base.

attacks.attack: The accuracy claim rests on a 2024 comparator with unrecorded output. 'As accurate as the frontier models' is supported only by 0.925 vs GPT-4o 0.880 (BOUNDED; only the number survives in FINDINGS.md); GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.x and Claude 5 were never run on those pages, Qwen3-VL's 96.1 is Qwen-reported, and the best specialist bar on olmOCR-Bench is 87.4 (Nanonets OCR-3), above the brief's 85.2 target.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Rerun modal_incumbent_docvqa.py with current frontier models (record accuracy and $/1K pages this time); olmOCR-Bench for full parse; kill gate 7 (trail by > 3 pts on both).

attacks.attack: The model half of the Morph playbook is entirely unproven: neither ledger contains a training result; the fine-tune must beat Nanonets 87.4 / Mistral 85.2 / dots.mocr 83.9 with ~50k synthetic pages from a frontier teacher (terms-of-service exposure) in a plan that allotted one week to data generation, pipeline and training. Relace's and olmOCR's recipes are external analogs, not evidence.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: LoRA-SFT 8B/4B on ~50k olmOCR-recipe pages (~$6k, ~40 GPU-h, three weeks), evaluated on olmOCR-Bench, DocVQA and a held-out extraction set; kill gate 6 (< base or < 82.4).

attacks.attack: Workload assumptions are unsupported by the research files: no document-API volume disclosures, no telemetry on batch-vs-interactive mix, no evidence buyers value per-page latency in agent loops, and no customer interviews in the repos. The 'pain' quotes are paraphrases. The two-lane scheduler is designed for a demand shape nobody measured.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Three design-partner pilots with logged s/page and lane usage; kill gate 9 (0 of 3 pilots use the agent lane). Outreach must start in week 1, not week 6.

attacks.attack: Instruction/schema prefix caching is overstated: the 12x number is for a 4k text prefix on a text model; in a VLM prompt only tokens before the first image are a shared prefix, a schema placed after the image is not cacheable, and a few-hundred-token instruction prefix saves milliseconds, not the 4k win.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: TTFT with and without APC on the real prompt template at 1024 px; report the cached fraction.

attacks.attack: Content-aware pruning is blocked (Qwen2.5-VL mRoPE; Qwen3-VL unknown) while model-level token compression already exists in the open (DeepSeek-OCR < 800 vision tokens; InternVL3.5 ViR ~50% fewer tokens). An engine-level pruner may be overtaken by base models that are natively token-efficient — the shelf-life risk the 'fast apply is dead' essay raised for Morph.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Qwen3-VL position-handling check and a matched-budget pruning-vs-resize sweep (gate 3); quarterly tracking of stock open-model s/page (gate 10).

attacks.attack: Evidence base is single-seed, single-GPU, 200 pages, one run, and the reusable platform code is thinner than 'gateway with 29 tests' implies: 7 of the tests are session-service tests, the Dockerfile omits control/, there is no streaming, rate limiting, payments or integration test against a live backend, and the voice load harness needs a tokenizer, aiohttp, server-metric scraping and multi-seed aggregation before it can drive this workload.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Three seeds x two GPUs for every headline; an integration test of gateway -> vLLM endpoint; the harness generalization list in 03-build-inventory.md completed before week 4.

attacks.attack: The 6-week plan slips on five identifiable lines: week 2 (spec-decode on VLM inputs may be engine work), week 3 (LLMEngine scheduler needs an HTTP serving loop; gateway image lacks control/), week 4 fine-tune in one week (50k teacher pages + pipeline + training), week 5 harness generalization, week 6 three signed pilots with zero prior conversations. Realistic: 8-10 weeks to the engine proof, 14-18 with the fine-tune.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: The calendar itself: the week-1 spec-decode smoke test and copy-fraction gate determine which branch (8-10 vs 14-18 weeks) applies.

missing_founder_decisions: Task choice: the draft selected document parse from seven Morph-style candidates (voice turn model, context compaction, agent-trace classifiers, code-search subagent, screenshot-diff perception, tool-call routing) on qualitative ratings; the founder should pick, or pick two tasks that share the speculator.
Engine base: vLLM 0.24.0 (ledger-pinned) vs SGLang (better at branched decode per the ledger's SGLang gate) vs a fork (Morph's Reflexes engine is 'forked from vLLM'); the draft assumed vLLM.
MVP shape: hosted per-page API first (vs BYOC-first or open-weights-first); the draft assumed hosted with a 10,000-page free tier copied from Unstructured.

Synthetic-data teacher and terms of service: the olmOCR recipe uses Claude Sonnet 4 at ~$0.12/page; frontier teacher vs open teacher (Qwen3-VL-235B) vs human-labeled subset; ~$6k budget assumed 50k pages.
Accuracy metric that buyers will be shown: relaxed-match DocVQA on 200 validation pages (the repo's) vs ANLS on test vs olmOCR-Bench vs a schema-extraction eval; the draft mixed them.
Kill-gate thresholds: 40%/70% copy fraction, 1.5x/2x speculation, 2x/3x throughput, 82.4/85.2 accuracy, $5/$1 per 1K COGS, 0/2 of 3 pilots were all chosen by the draft and need ratification.
Team size and calendar: the 6-week plan implicitly assumes 1-2 engineers plus GPU budget; the realistic 8-10 (engine) or 14-18 (with fine-tune) week calendar depends on it.
First GPU class: A100-80GB (matches the ledger) vs H100 (the GPU buyers benchmark on) vs MI355X ($2.29-$2.95/hr per Wafer); the draft chose A100 first.
Model size and base: Qwen3-VL-8B vs 4B vs 2B vs dots.mocr 3B vs olmOCR-2-7B; the draft defaulted to 8B.
Parse-first vs extract-first SKU: parse has public benchmarks and a higher expected copy fraction; extract has $20-$50/1K price points.
Speculator form: prompt-lookup only (buyer-replicable) vs trained draft head (Morph's differentiator); the draft assumed both.
Whether to publish the harness and benchmark openly (Wafer-style) or not (Morph's benchmark pages returned HTTP 429 in research).
Whether the first public proof is the engine alone (stock Qwen3-VL-8B, 8-10 weeks) or engine plus fine-tuned model (14-18 weeks).
Third-party listing (e.g., OpenRouter) as an independent throughput check, which the draft assumed 'if available'.
strongest_version: A per-page document-parse API built on an open 4B-8B VLM, where the company's proprietary work is (a) a task-trained draft head that exploits the copy-like structure of parse output, (b) a page-shaped engine with batch and latency lanes and a visual-token budgeter, and (c) a fine-tuned model evaluated on public benchmarks with a rerunnable harness — all sold in the unit buyers already use, against per-page list prices from $1.50 to $50 per 1,000 pages. The in-repo evidence supports only the economics precondition: an open 7B at 1024 px matched a 2024 frontier model on 200 short-answer pages at 2.7x its own higher-resolution throughput, in-engine, on an A100. Everything Morph-specific — copy fraction, copy speculation, the trained speculator, engine-level pruning, the fine-tune, full-page throughput under load — is unmeasured, and the first two weeks decide whether a well-configured vLLM already captures the gain. If gates 1-4 pass, the company has a measured engine advantage on a workload with public benchmarks, Apache-2.0 bases and a published data recipe, and can publish a proof buyers can rerun. If gates 2 and 4 fail, the honest fallback is a fine-tuned-model-plus-per-page-pricing company, which the founder must weigh against Reducto r-1, Mistral OCR 4 and the open OCR models as facts, not verdicts.
changes_made: Moved 'accuracy parity vs GPT-4o (0.925 vs 0.880)' from Proven to Bounded per ledger status, with the unrecorded-output, GPT-4o-mini-unrecorded and 2024-comparator caveats; added a current-frontier rerun to Unproven and a new kill gate (7).

Redefined proof baseline (1) as a well-configured vLLM (same max_pixels, prefix caching, FP8, built-in n-gram speculation if it accepts image inputs) so the buyer-replicable 2.7x resize cannot count toward the 3x target; added kill gate 2 (baseline erases the lever).
Added the unverified dependency on vLLM's speculative-decoding path accepting Qwen3-VL image inputs as an explicit unproven claim, a week-2 slip risk, and part of kill gate 4.

Stated on every use that the 30.2 img/s / 2.7x number is one offline LLM.chat batch at max_tokens=32 (not a served endpoint, not full-page parse), single run, single GPU, no seeds; flagged that no full-page parse measurement exists in either repo.

Corrected the pricing floor: the repo's '$0.02-0.06 / 1k pages' is a hardcoded string; the $0.023/1K derivation is field-QA only; added the ~11 s per 500-token page single-stream implication and moved margin claims to 'must be confirmed'.
Renamed 'schema-prefix cache' to 'instruction-prefix cache' with the constraint that only pre-image tokens are cacheable and that the 12x figure is for a 4k text prefix.

Fixed the competitive table: Azure disconnected containers and Google custom-processor hosting (draft said 'no BYOC'); removed the unsupported Baseten Qwen3-VL hosting implication; added Nanonets OCR-3 87.4 and Chandra 83.1; added DeepSeek-OCR/InternVL3.5 model-level token compression as facts.
Removed the misattributed 'mRoPE blocker' from the screenshot-diff row and compressed the task-selection table into a 'Task choice' founder decision.

Added omitted ledger caveats: decode reference is eager/prefix-caching-off/gen=64/one run; gateway's 29 tests include 7 session tests and the Dockerfile omits control/; voice evidence is single-seed, L40S, synthetic, 27.8 ms margin; Qwen3-VL numbers are Qwen-reported; both repos are single-seed for every headline.

Rewrote the 6-week plan with slip risks (spec-decode engine work, HTTP serving loop for the LLMEngine scheduler, three-week fine-tune, harness generalization list, pilot outreach from week 1) and added a realistic 8-10 / 14-18 week calendar.

Added kill gates for current-frontier parity, well-configured baseline, spec-decode feasibility, seed/GPU replication, and base-model shelf life driven by token-efficient architectures; merged pruning into the prefill-bound gate.

Expanded founder decisions with task choice, engine base, synthetic-data teacher/ToS, accuracy metric, team size, kill-gate ratification, free tier and pricing unit; merged market-size and adjacency into one 'not judged' item with the facts listed neutrally.

Deleted words to meet the 3,500-word cap: dropped the Deployables and CUA-analog bullets, the Extend/LlamaParse and Wafer/Relace/Cognition table rows, two combination bullets and one pain quote; no numbers were changed in the process.
